result.keywords: Braitenberg vehicles provide a compact framework for linking sensory inputs to adaptive motion in autonomous systems. Here, a hybrid memristive platform combining reconfigurable nanowire junctions with simple neuromorphic circuits is presented to realize a hardware Braitenberg controller that can alter its sensor-motor couplings during operation. The device exhibits both reweighting and rewiring effects under electrical stimulation, enabling path following, obstacle avoidance, and rapid response to changing stimulus patterns. By integrating structural plasticity with low-latency memristive dynamics, the proposed system offers a scalable route toward self-adaptive robots and unconventional computing architectures capable of learning from multiple environmental cues.
result.title: Reconfigurable Braitenberg Navigation via Self-Organizing Memristive Nanowire Circuits.
